key_insight: Projected-Block Van Vleck Perturbation Theory (PB-VVPT) efficiently predicts quantum-state transfer in molecular polaritonic networks while retaining phonon-driven decoherence and memory effects.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support computationally efficient design and evaluation of cavity-coupled molecular networks for quantum information transfer.
method: Model molecules, an optical cavity, and local phonons with a generalized Holstein–Tavis–Cummings Hamiltonian.
Use quasidegenerate perturbation theory to construct fixed-phonon-number sectors and coupled polaron–polariton subblocks.
Compute coherence and population propagators without a Markovian approximation.
evidence_signal: Against exact molecular-wheel dynamics, PB-VVPT reproduced molecule-to-molecule and molecule-to-cavity transfer with errors below 1% over most simulated intervals and an estimated diagonalization cost over 100× lower.
watch_item: Validation is limited to simulated molecular-wheel networks in the nonadiabatic, weak exciton–phonon coupling regime; broader applicability remains to be established.
paper_title: Quantum Information Transfer in Molecular Polaritonic Networks: A Van Vleck Effective-Hamiltonian Approach
